questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university was academically sound in my field of study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the host university and UCPH combined provided all necessary information in due time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My host institution provided a lot of options for obligatory and unobligatory events and information gatherings in a timely and non-overwhelming way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very tough. Search wide, but it is ok to start searching (intensely) first *after* not receiving university-provided housing.
I started searching before the university announced if I had received housing through them, and accepted a lease before finding out that university-provided housing had been granted to me, but at that time I was locked in on my contract, which was inferior to the one that the university provided.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everybody lives off campus and the university is aware of this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They announced housing-distribution pretty late in summer which is nerve-wracking.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a little though finding courses and finding whether the exam could be taken when comming from abroad (e.g. due to travelling home before exam date). The professors where quick to answer questions in regards to exams and distance-examinations preponement of exams. A bit unclear sometimes whether exhange students could follow a specific course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy and flexible. Could switch up untill a week into the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online platforms primarely.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took a lot of time finding a schedule that didn't overlap, which was very imortant for me. I found 30 ETCS and was ultimately very happy with the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to students at the university and look for off-uni means of checking grade-statistics and difficulty/comments from previous students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very tough to adapt to the ways of the host university. Exam forms were different which adds difficulty.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
16 credits MA, 8 credits BA. Remaining 6 credits where non-compulsory courses that could be taken in BA/MA programs.
Ultimately, the difficulty of all courses were interchangable. The BA course was just as tough as the MA courses (if not more so, actually, but it is probably very subject specific).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar in lectures, but exercise sessions were very different. Less contact with TA's and likewise less academic support in genneral.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Algorithms, Probability, and Computing (8)
Network Security (8)
Concepts of Object Oriented Programming (8)
Wireless Networking and Mobile Computing (4)
Technology Entrepreneurship (2)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Technology Entrepreneurship was a very nice and relexaing course while still being *very* inspiring. Easy exam
Network Security is probably one of (if not *the*) best course I have ever followed. Great and satisfying content. Excellent lecturers and mostly good guest lecturers. A bit of a funky exam but easy to pass due to projects that give part of the final grade.

Housing DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of micro-transactions in Switzerland and transport is *very* efficient, but also **very** expensive so beware and by the half-tax travelcard early on - even if for half a year use.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets are very expensive but not so much more than in Denmark if care is taken.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Free fitness was amazing!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN provided some social events early on which was very nice to get to know fellow exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hikes, hikes, hikes, some of the amazing cities of Switzerland.
Skiing if you are into that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains or meet with friends. Be strict with your self in how you divide work and pleasure. You need to also work on at least some weekends to survive most likely.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy and similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Initiate the conversation. Nobody is going to talk  to you explicitly. It is your responsibility to get out there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The genneral ideology is a bit different from the danish. It is not common to drink a beer after a days work - not even on fridays unless previously established.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How efficient society is and day-to-day politeness of Swiss people. Easy to integrate as a Danish person.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get out there early on and meet new people.
Be very cautious of the difficulty level of the courses you choose.
Download Tinder if lonely (it helped)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Always remember how big a priviledge it is to be able to study and learn.
Remember to hit the fitness.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Being able to pass the courses and still succeeding in accomplishing my goals with my trip.
You don't go to ETH for extra leasure time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing the study load with my ambitions for the exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Keep a cool head and remember that passing the course is all that is needed!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
